title: OrbitPay burst failover timing regression causing reserved-pool shortfalls
creator: Rajiv Kapoor
description:
Summary:

OrbitPay experienced repeated capacity shortfalls during a high-volume billing window (2025-02-09 13:00-15:30 UTC). Customers observed 5xx throttles and request queuing despite available GPUs in the region. This ticket tracks the investigation, hotfix, rollout, and follow-ups.

What happened:
- During a tenant-level burst, the Dedicated autoscaler paused decisioning for a 2-6 minute window for multiple reserved pools in us-west-2. While the infra showed idle slots, the pool allocator rejected burst allocations and allowed tenant burst credits to be decremented without reconciliation. The combined effect surfaced as apparent capacity shortfall at the API layer and triggered OrbitPay escalations to support.

Key user impact:
- OrbitPay lost request throughput for paid customers for ~2.5 hours including repeated short outages during recovery attempts. Latency spiked, and some long-running requests returned 503. Support and CSM engaged; revenue-impacting. Classified as high customer_impact.

Investigation notes / timeline:
- 2025-02-09 15:45 UTC: OrbitPay alerted via support channel; on-call routed to infra.
- 2025-02-09 16:05 UTC: Initial mitigation applied: temporarily increased reserved pool headroom for affected tenant which allowed immediate short-term recovery.
- 2025-02-10: Deep dive started by autoscaler, allocator, and runtime teams. Correlated Grafana panels (link below) showed a cluster-wide pause in autoscaler evaluate() cycles coincident with etcd snapshot uploads and leader rebalancing.
- 2025-02-11: Reproduced locally with network partition test harness: when control-plane snapshotting overlapped leader re-election, the evaluate loop skipped scale-up decisions for entires with pending KV-cache reconciliation.
- 2025-02-12: Discovered a rounding/overflow edge-case in burst credit accounting which allowed credits to drop negative in rare interleavings; negative credits were processed by allocator as "exhausted" even when headroom existed.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) Autoscaler evaluate loop could be paused when the control-plane leader is in snapshotting state or when a race occurs during leader handover, leaving the allocator state stale for minutes.
2) A separate burst-credit accounting bug (integer rounding and an unchecked negative delta) meant the system sometimes marked tenants as out-of-credits even after the headroom increase, preventing allocations from being accepted.

Immediate actions taken: (hotfixes and mitigations)
- Hotfix published: runtime-1.20.1 containing: 
  - Guard around evaluate() to continue decisioning during snapshot windows (non-blocking snapshot io).
  - Credit-reconciliation safety net: if credit balance < 0 && pool has positive available slots, reconcile by creating a temporary credit buffer for 60s.
  - Defensive checks to prevent negative-credit acceptance paths.
- Canary rollout started 2025-02-15 in us-west-2 (10% of traffic) -> observed no repeat of the 2-6 minute pause on canary hosts.
- Full rollout to dedicated fleet completed 2025-02-18 04:10 UTC.

PRs and artifacts:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-autoscaler/pull/2543
- Credit reconciliation patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pool-allocator/pull/788
- Incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/autoscaler-orbitpay-incident?orgId=1
- Postmortem draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/54321/OrbitPay+incident+2025-02-09
- Customer ticket: https://support.redwood.com/tickets/ORBIT-984

Current status:
- Hotfix rolled out; monitoring shows error rate returned to baseline for OrbitPay and other tenants in the region.
- OrbitPay confirmed traffic normalized and accepted interim credits for impacted requests.
- Root cause validated in staging; will be finalized in postmortem.

Remaining work / follow-ups (owner in parentheses):
- Implement long-term leader-resilience changes in autoscaler (ENG: Maya Chen).
- Add unit + integration tests for credit rounding and negative balance safety (ENG: Tomasz Nowak).
- Expand canary policy to test snapshot+leader handover overlap scenarios in CI (ENG: Platform Reliability).
- Update runbook to include headroom emergency guidance and customer comms template for reserved-pool shortfalls (Ops: Lina Rodriguez).
- Run a 72-hour soak test for runtime-1.20.1 under synthetic burst traffic (QA: Leah Murphy).

Communication and reviews:
- PM and CSM review completed; CSM draft sent to OrbitPay 2025-02-16.
- Security reviewed hotfix surface area; no new secrets or exposure (security_review_required: false).

Notes and trade-offs:
- The temporary credit buffer mitigates immediate customer impact but adds a small window where burst accounting is permissive; it is intentionally time-limited (60s) and logged for audit.
- We prioritized a fast non-invasive fix to restore customer traffic; the longer-term leader-resilience change will require refactoring of election and snapshot semantics and is scheduled as follow-up.

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket:
- ORBIT customer verifies stable service for 7 days post-rollout (CSM confirmation).
- Unit/integration tests added and merged for credit-edge cases.
- Runbook updated and a tabletop run completed with SRE and Support.
- Postmortem published and linked in this ticket.

Postmortem link (final): TODO - attach when complete.
updates: 2025-02-10: Triage started; assigned to Maya Chen. Initial mitigation applied to OrbitPay pool headroom.
2025-02-11: Repro harness created showing evaluate() pause during leader handover + snapshot overlap.
2025-02-12: Found negative-credit race; drafted reconciliation patch.
2025-02-15: Canary rollout of runtime-1.20.1 (10%) — no regression observed on canaries.
2025-02-18: Full rollout completed; monitoring shows stable error rates. Pending follow-ups remain.
